mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, signaled by a positive YoY change in real GDP, predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as rising aggregate demand boosts corporate revenues and profits.
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns are negative > 40% of the time following positive YoY GDPC1 growth, or the mechanism's Rank IC falls below 0.05 in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) over 3 months, indicating supply chain disruptions, leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as companies struggle with input shortages and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 60-day returns in > 55% of instances following a 2%+ 3-month drop in INDPRO, or the mechanism's Rank IC is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market and slowing economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors reassess downside risks.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive > 45% of the time following a 0.3pp+ rise in UNRATE over 2 months, or the mechanism's Rank IC is negative in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4%, indicating a restrictive monetary policy stance, S&P 500 returns tend to be negative over the next 60 trading days as higher borrowing costs weigh on economic activity and equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive > 40% of the time when FEDFUNDS > 4%, or the mechanism's Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise by more than 5% YoY, signaling a strong residential construction cycle, S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 20 trading days as the housing boom boosts economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative > 35% of the time following a 5%+ YoY rise in HOUST, or the mechanism's Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200k jobs per month for 3 consecutive months, signaling a strong labor market, S&P 500 returns are positive over the next 60 trading days as the tight labor market boosts wage growth and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows > 200k per month for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative > 40% of the time following 3 consecutive months of 200k+ PAYEMS growth, or the mechanism's Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When real retail sales (RSAFS) decline by more than 2% YoY, signaling a consumer spending slowdown, S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 20 trading days as investors reassess the growth outlook and equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive > 45% of the time following a 2%+ YoY decline in RSAFS, or the mechanism's Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 3% YoY, signaling high inflation, and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, indicating a tightening monetary policy response, S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 trading days as the inflation-squeeze on consumer spending and the Fed's hawkish stance weigh on economic growth and equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive > 40% of the time when CPIAUCSL is up > 3% YoY and FEDFUNDS > 2%, or the mechanism's Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.
